procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism through its Factory Registration service; registration requires the factory to be outside a free zone, an industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Include in the application the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately.

Apply through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents, pay the fee online, submit the application and print the approved certificate.
Pay the certificate fee, which is estimated at AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100,000 (the fee range is AED 10 to AED 200).
The certificate must be issued before, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for twelve months from issue and covers only one import.
Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India; if a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed.
Keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The agreement does not define '+' in the rule; Mansha interprets it as 'and' (both tests must pass).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The certificate fee estimate assumes the invoice value equals the shipment value given.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
The agreement says box 8 for the certificate, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 read through LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
An invoice issued by a third party does not by itself cause the claim to be denied; the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating.
